expl: The Human Development Report is published every year by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is released by considering three major dimensions of human development—per capita gross national income (in PPP terms), literacy rate, and life expectancy at birth—which correspond to a decent standard of living, knowledge, and a long and healthy life. stem:
Human capital formation as a concept is better explained in terms of a process, which enables
1. individuals of a country to accumulate more capital
2. increasing the knowledge
3. increasing the skill levels
4. increasing the knowledge, skill levels and capacities of the people of the country
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
expl: Investment in education transforms humans into human capital. Thus, human capital represents increased productivity. It is an acquired ability and the result of well-considered investment decisions, made with the expectation of increasing future sources of income. Investment in education, workplace training, health, migration and information are sources of human capital formation.

the atmanirbhar Bharat Scheme announced by the Government helps in:
(1) Enhancing india's manufacturing capabilities and exports across the industries
(2) incentivizing foreign investments for domestic production out of these:
expl: The declared objective of Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan is to increase domestic manufacturing capacity and develop India as a global supply chain and export hub. stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Svamitva scheme :
1. it is a Central Sector Scheme under the ministry of mines.
2. this scheme seeks to create geo-positioning infrastructure like CorS network to benchmark the location and provides five centimetre level accuracy.
3. CorS means Cross-origin resource Sharing.
4. the scheme is a reformatory step towards establishment of clear ownership of property in rural inhabited (abadi) areas, by mapping of land parcels using drone technology.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
expl: Started in April 2020, the full name of the SVAMITVA scheme is: SVAMITVA – Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas. It is a Central Sector Scheme. The objective of this scheme is to provide an integrated property verification solution for rural India by using the latest drone survey technology to demarcate inhabited (abadi) land in rural areas. Under this scheme, there is a provision to establish the CORS (Continuously Operating Reference Stations) network, which is an important activity for accurate georeferencing, geoverification, and demarcation of land.

stem: What is the objective of the 'Pradhan mantri Shram Yogi maandhan Yojana' announced in Budget 2019-20?

options.label: a
options.text: Providing education allowance for a single girl child

options.label: c
options.text: Providing pension benefits to retail traders and small shopkeepers

expl: Pradhan Mantri ShramYogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme started by the Central Government to provide social security to workers of the unorganised sector. This scheme ensures a minimum monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60 years to those unorganised sector workers whose monthly income is up to Rs. 15,000. The scheme is meant for unorganised sector workers, who contribute about 50 percent to the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). PM-SYM was introduced in the Interim Budget 2019-20. The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Labour and Employment with the support of the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and Common Service Centre e-Governance Services India Limited (CSC SPV) for seamless implementation. Pm-SYm (Pm-SYm) Key Features • The Central Government contributes on a 1:1 basis, equal to the worker’s contribution. • This is a voluntary scheme, allowing workers to contribute as per their capacity and requirement. • If the beneficiary dies, the spouse gets 50 percent of the pension amount as family pension. Family pension is available only to the spouse. • Participants may exit the scheme subject to specified conditions (as detailed in Section 9). • Eligible workers can register through Common Service Centres (CSCs) or through the Maandhan portal. • The scheme is administered by LIC, ensuring financial stability and reliability.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The all-round development of any community—such as physical, social, moral, and cultural development—is called “community development” (Community Development). Community development includes all important elements of life such as agriculture, animal husbandry, irrigation, cooperatives, education, health, social productive activities, communication, village industries, panchayats, etc. According to the United Nations, “Community development denotes the processes by which the efforts of the people themselves are united with those of governmental authorities to improve the economic, social and cultural conditions of communities, to integrate these communities into the life of the nation, and to enable them to contribute fully to national progress.”

stem:
Consider the following Schemes :
i. EaS
ii. trYSEm
iii. JrY
iv. rlEGP the correct chronological sequence of the launching of these schemes is :
expl: The TRYSEM (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment) scheme was started in August 1979 with the objective of providing training for self-employment to rural youth in the 18–35 years age group. The RLEGP (Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme) was started on 15 August 1983 to provide employment opportunities to the rural landless. By merging the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP), the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) was started in April 1989. The Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) was started on 2 October 1993. Its main objective was to provide employment to rural youth suffering from seasonal unemployment.

expl: The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in the Union Budget Speech, 2022–23. Through this scheme, such border villages on the northern border—where the population is very sparse, connectivity and basic facilities are very limited, and which have been deprived of the benefits of development—will be brought under this new programme. Activities under it include basic village facilities, housing, development of tourism centres, road connectivity, arrangement of decentralised renewable energy, direct-to-home access for Doordarshan and educational channels, and support for livelihood generation, etc. Additional funds will be provided for these activities. On 15 February 2023, the Government of India approved Vibrant Village Programme-I for the comprehensive development of selected villages in 46 blocks of 19 districts adjoining the northern border in Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, and the Union Territory of Ladakh.

stem: Which one of the following is the objective of mGnrEGa?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The main objective of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is to provide 100 days of employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual work related to public works, at the statutory minimum wage rate. Its other objectives include rural development, under which durable assets such as roads, canals, ponds, and wells are generally created. Works such as construction and repair of embankments, land levelling, plantation, water conservation and harvesting, and flood control and protection can also be included under this scheme. In the background of wide-ranging changes in MGNREGA, the Central Government has notified the “Viksit Bharat— Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, 2025.” This law provides a guarantee of 125 days in a financial year to such rural households whose members are willing to do unskilled work.

stem:
CPm includes child malnutrition as a proxy for lack of health and nourishment.
2. Female illiteracy is included to reflect deprivation in education and knowledge.
3. it considers male illiteracy as a key indicator of capability poverty.
4. it includes lack of access to clean drinking water as an important indicator of capability poverty.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In the Human Development Report, 1996, UNDP introduced a composite index called the “Capability Poverty Measure (CPM),” which measures deprivation in three basic human capabilities— 1. The capability to live a healthy and well-nourished life, 2. The capability of healthy reproduction, and The capability to be educated and knowledgeable. Under this, child malnutrition (the proportion of children under five years of age who are underweight) has been included to indicate deprivation in health and nutrition. To measure deprivation in education and knowledge, CPM uses “the percentage of illiterate women aged 15 years and above” as an indicator. Male illiteracy is not treated as an indicator in CPM. Only statements 1 and 2 match the official definition of CPM, while statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.

stem: as per nFHS-5 data, which of the following state(s) recorded less than 6% of the population as multidimensionally poor in 2019-20?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the NFHS-5 based headcount ratio, the multidimensional poverty rate of the given States/Union Territories is as follows— Jammu and Kashmir (4.80%), Himachal Pradesh (4.93%), and Uttar Pradesh (22.93%). Thus, both Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have a multidimensional poverty rate below 6%. Since Jammu and Kashmir is a Union Territory, therefore, from the point of view of “states,” Himachal Pradesh will be the correct answer. Among all the States/Union Territories of India, the highest multidimensional poverty rate is recorded in Bihar (33.76%). It may be noted that NFHS-5 data pertains to 2019–21, whereas the question mentions 2019–20.

stem: Which statement is not true about the poverty estimates based on the 68th round of nSSo?

options.label: a
options.text: The poverty line defined at `27.20 per capita per day for rural areas.

options.label: d
options.text: The 33.35 per cent population of India was living below the poverty line.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: On the basis of the findings of the report released by the Tendulkar Committee, for the year 2011-12, at the all-India level, the poverty line was estimated as consumption expenditure of Rs. 816 per person per month (Rs. 27.20 per day) for rural areas, and Rs. 1000 per person per month (Rs. 33.33 per day) for urban areas. In 2011-12, the percentage of persons living below the poverty line was recorded as 25.7 percent in rural areas, 13.7 percent in urban areas, and 21.9 percent at the all-India level. It is noteworthy that for the reference year 2011-12, the data were released as monthly consumption expenditure, not as daily figures. In this question, the month has been taken as equivalent to 30 days, and the explanation has been done accordingly.

stem:
according to the Planning Commission of india, which of the following are correct for the poverty line?
i. rs. 42 per capita per day in urban area
ii. rs. 26 per capita per day in rural area
iii. rs. 32 per capita per day in urban area
iv. rs. 32 per capita per day in rural area
Choose the correct option from the following :
expl: Using the data of the NSSO Household Consumer Expenditure Survey and as per the recommendations of the Tendulkar Committee, the Planning Commission updated the poverty ratio and poverty lines for 2011-12 and released the poverty estimates for 2011-12 in July 2013. According to these, in 2011-12, at the all-India level, the poverty line was recorded as consumption expenditure of Rs. 816 per person per month (Rs. 26.32 per day) for rural areas and Rs. 1000 per person per month (Rs. 32.25 per day) for urban areas. Therefore, as the nearest correct answer, option (c) can be selected. note- Here, the month has been taken as equivalent to 31 days.
